name: Tree-fall alarm
subtitle: hears a city tree before it falls

effects.effect: wood fibres tearing under strain give off bursts of tiny clicks

effect: wood fibres tearing under strain give off bursts of tiny clicks
how: Falling trees and branches kill people in storms and bring down power lines, yet a rotten trunk often looks healthy. As wood fibres start to tear in the wind, the trunk gives off bursts of clicks far too faint to hear; a sensor screwed into the trunk counts them during gusts and radios the city when one tree clicks far more than its neighbours, so it can be braced or felled first.
obstacle: Knowing which click rates mean real danger needs years of recordings from trees that actually fell.
why: Turns hidden rot into a warning that protects people, roads and power lines.
real: Fraunhofer IKTS and the TreeMon project are developing trunk-mounted acoustic-emission sensor nodes that count wind-induced fibre fractures for tree safety, but no validated failure-warning system yet.
